1. Introduction: The Identity of the Clamshell Protecting Satellites

Look up at the tip of a rocket. There, you will find a part called a "fairing," which looks like a giant clamshell. This fairing acts as a "shield" that protects the delicate artificial satellite stored inside from the harsh environment until the rocket reaches space.
During launch, the satellite is exposed to three major threats that are unimaginable on the ground.

: The immense force of air encountered when pushing through the atmosphere at hypersonic speeds. Imagine leaning out of the window of a car traveling at thousands of kilometers per hour. Pressure hundreds of times greater than that strikes the satellite.

: The tremendous vibration caused by the roar of the rocket engines. It is like placing precision equipment right in front of a giant live speaker, with the risk that intense sound wave vibrations could destroy electronic circuits.
